A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VT-DIS research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original sampling experiments, ESS and computational-cost measurements, distribution plots, and covariance and divergence analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds likelihood-bound results, stochastic-trace PF-ODE comparisons, and ALDP failure checks.

M1.justification: The frozen score network, covariance parameterizations, alpha=2 objective, and trajectory importance weighting remain unchanged. V2 documents log-space loss computation for numerical stability; this does not establish a new method component or a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GMM-2 in 50 and 100 dimensions, DW-4, LJ-13, and alanine dipeptide at 800 K. The additions use these same targets without introducing different tasks, populations, or input conditions.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix D.1 and Table 5 add PF-ODE importance sampling with Hutchinson trace estimation using one or ten probes. DDPM+IS and exact PF-ODE+IS remain. Newly discussed energy-only neural samplers are explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E3.justification: V2 adds ELBO/EUBO evaluation, one-versus-ten-probe PF-ODE settings, and ALDP DDPM tests at 1,000 and 2,000 steps. These extend the evaluation protocol; the previously reported dataset splits, architectures, training budgets, and main comparison settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted checks of ALDP's persistent forward-ESS failure at much larger step counts and examines the ESS/cost tradeoff across trace-probe counts. The optimized-covariance and KL-versus-alpha=2 analyses already appear in v1 Appendix D.1–D.2 and remain as v2 D.2–D.3.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 3 explicitly reports error bars as one standard deviation across three repeated Monte Carlo evaluations. V1 already displays mean/standard-deviation ESS results, but provides no corresponding repeat count. This addition does not establish more training runs or changed uncertainty practices for retained results.

E6.justification: Under the same stated Table 1 setting, ALDP exact PF-ODE forward ESS changes from 34.81% to approximately zero, substantially revising its apparent coverage advantage. V2 also adds ELBO/EUBO results across DW-4, LJ-13, and ALDP, stochastic PF-ODE ESS/cost results in Table 5, and near-zero forward ESS at 1,000–2,000 ALDP DDPM steps.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 replaces v1's equality between D2 and the integral loss with equality of their minimizers, adding the normalized alpha-divergence definition. This distinguishes D2=(L−1)/2 from L. The importance-sampling derivations and equivariance proofs in Appendices A–B are retained.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain covariance-only post-training, efficient trajectory importance sampling, an equivariant extension, and improved ESS at low inference cost. Removing 'lightweight' and explicitly specifying inference-time overhead do not materially change those claims; the abstract's headline ESS values are unchanged.

C2.justification: V1 leaves ALDP's near-zero forward ESS largely unresolved. V2 substantially develops the missing-mode hypothesis, explains why covariance tuning cannot reliably repair inadequate score-model coverage, and states corresponding applicability limits. It also explicitly identifies the reference-sample requirement and replaces the weak-coordinate-correlation explanation with discussion of a slight full-covariance advantage.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and Appendix C.1's explicit logsumexp implementation of the loss. Existing hardware specifications, data sizes, architectures, optimizer settings, and training/sampling runtime tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds energy-only neural samplers and reasons for excluding them, supported by new citations. It removes the consistency-model sampling discussion and associated references, and narrows the expensive-likelihood criticism to CNFs. The central positioning against KL-based covariance tuning remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites to related work, experimental setup, and ALDP discussion, while preserving most prose and the main section sequence. It adds objective-implementation and PF-ODE appendix subsections and a Broader Impacts appendix, with corresponding renumbering and updated front matter.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into the TMLR style, changing typography, margins, author layout, running headers, and figure/table placement. V2 adds the three-panel likelihood-bound Figure 3 and comparison Table 5. Earlier Figures 3–6 are retained as Figures 4–7 rather than representing new analyses.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation and reproducibility through likelihood-bound results, practical PF-ODE trace comparisons with explicit bias caveats, and code and loss-implementation information. The revised ALDP result weakens the earlier PF-ODE coverage finding, but the accompanying failure checks and clearer applicability limits improve transparency. These are useful, targeted improvements; the proposed missing-mode explanation remains a hypothesis.
